slides.title: Music as Universal Language
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 8 English, Unit 9: Music as Universal Language. This unit is called "Music as Universal Language" because you will explore how music, performance, and the creative arts bring people together across cultures, languages, and backgrounds. Music is one of the most powerful forms of human expression. It can communicate emotions that words alone cannot capture. A song can make you feel joy, sorrow, excitement, or peace without you understanding a single word of the language in which it is sung. That is why we call music a universal language: it speaks to everyone. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Explain what it means to call music a universal language and discuss how the performing arts connect people across cultures.
Read the story "The Curtain Never Lies" and answer comprehension and analysis questions using evidence from the text.
Use thirty key vocabulary words related to performance, creativity, emotion, and integrity in your own speaking and writing.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to explain what it means to call music a universal language and discuss how the performing arts connect people across cultures. You will also read the story "The Curtain Never Lies" and answer comprehension and analysis questions using evidence from the text. You will also use thirty key vocabulary words related to performance, creativity, emotion, and integrity in your own speaking and writing. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: havoc, deft, render, muster, deploy, gait. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: What Makes Music a Universal Language?
Behind the Curtain: How a School Production Comes Together
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes What Makes Music a Universal Language? and Behind the Curtain: How a School Production Comes Together. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Present Perfect Continuous
bullets: The Present Perfect Continuous describes actions that began in the past and are still running now, or that have only just stopped and left visible...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Present Perfect Continuous. The Present Perfect Continuous describes actions that began in the past and are still running now, or that have only just stopped and left visible evidence, as when paint-stained hands tell you someone has been painting. It is built with has or have, then been, then the -ing form of the verb, and it puts the spotlight on how long an activity has lasted rather than on whether it finished. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.
